A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UrbanGraph and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. The original model and experiments can be matched across versions, including relocated appendix material.

before.justification: Tables 1-2 and Appendices E-F report original microclimate prediction experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds simulator validation against measurements, city-scale validation, additional controls and wind-vector prediction results.

M1.justification: The original five-relation microclimate graph and RGCN-LSTM predictor remain substantially unchanged. Appendix G.2 adds a fluid-specific adaptation using directed advection edges and building-to-wake edges, focusing graph construction on fluid mechanisms.

E1.justification: V2 retains UMC4/12 and its six targets but adds NUS sensor measurements for simulator validation, Singapore-wide comparison against HiGTS, and UWF3D velocity-component prediction. These extend evaluation beyond the original simulated microclimate blocks to observational references and a distinct vector-field task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the original comparators and adds Pix2Pix+PINN, STGCN, ASTGCN and LRGCN. Appendix G additionally evaluates a Grid-GCN control against the adapted UrbanGraph. These are reported comparisons, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: New protocols include five-station simulator validation, aggregated HiGTS comparison for May 3, 2023, a 64x64 Grid-GCN control, physics-injection controls, shared-encoder multitask evaluation and a 36-window scalability test. The original 70/20/10 split and main training settings remain; the spatially unseen-block description newly clarifies the split without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a comparison of data-only, soft-physics and structural-physics approaches, single-task versus multitask learning, and reconstruction timing for approximately 90,000 nodes. Appendix B.2 adds external validation analyses. The original temporal, fusion, initialization, feature, edge and sensitivity ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Figure A3 newly reports station-wise Pearson correlations and significance thresholds. Existing three-trial reporting, standard deviations and confidence bands remain; no increase in the stated repeated-run count is established.

E6.justification: The retained main UrbanGraph scores remain R²=0.8542 and RMSE=1.0535, and the five auxiliary-target scores persist in expanded Table A13. V2 adds MAE values, comparator and control results, city-scale correlation r=0.842, and velocity-component R² values of 0.8886, 0.8474 and 0.7937 in Table A14. The convergence plot also replaces training/validation results with test-set results.

T1.justification: Appendix G and Figure A12 add formal inlet, symmetry, wall and outlet boundary conditions for the CFD benchmark. Existing graph, network, ENVI-met and edge-weight equations (1)-(17) remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes integrating heterogeneous and dynamic physics-informed graphs. V2 makes hard causal topology, prevention of spurious correlations and physical-operator decoupling central contributions. Its abstract and conclusion replace the 17% FLOPs headline with 73.8% fewer FLOPs and 21% lower training time relative to LRGCN, while framing applicability around dynamics governed by known physical equations.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving operator decoupling, reduced over-smoothing, Markovian transport as motivation for LSTM, and negative transfer in multitask learning. It interprets the new validations as evidence of broader robustness. The limitations retain concerns about predefined physics but replace generic adaptive graph learning with a proposed physical topology plus learnable residual graph.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies feature contents, source-map resolution and spatial holdout, and documents sensor forcing, city-validation aggregation, OpenFOAM/RANS configuration, geometry, inflow, mesh sizes and fluid-edge construction. The scalability test specifies 16 CPU workers. These substantially expand technical documentation; the original hyperparameter table and code/data availability disclosure remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work substantially repositions UrbanGraph as a structural inductive bias relative to observational inputs, soft PDE losses and implicit graph learning. New references support STGCN/ASTGCN comparisons, HiGTS validation and physical threshold choices; Banerjee et al. and Yan et al. are removed. The LRGCN paper was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, results discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten around the causal-topology framing. Dynamic and static edge descriptions are reordered, appendix subsections are expanded, and author and publication headers are reformatted.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1, replaces the convergence panel, adds input/prediction and validation figures, and introduces the vector-field illustration. Figure A1 expands from two displayed sites to ten. Table 1 gains category grouping, comparator rows and an MAE column, while new control and vector-result tables are added. Many original appendix heatmaps are simply relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for applicability beyond the original UMC4/12 experiments through broader comparisons, field checks of the simulator, HiGTS validation and a distinct vector-field task. Added controls also make architectural choices more assessable. Reporting problems temper these gains: LRGCN is mislabeled as the strongest baseline despite Table 1, and the field-validation text overstates several wind correlations shown in Figure A3. These problems limit the stronger claims but do not outweigh the substantial expansion of relevant empirical support.
